name: Applications
blurb: Field experiments and adoption studies on what AI actually does to output in real organisations.

papers.note: The most cited education position paper, and the source of the competency and literacy framing now used in policy.
papers.title: ChatGPT for good? On opportunities and challenges of large language models for education

papers.note: Preregistered experiment, 40 percent time reduction and 18 percent quality gain on professional writing tasks.
papers.title: Experimental evidence on the productivity effects of generative artificial intelligence

papers.note: 5,172 support agents, 15 percent productivity gain concentrated in less experienced workers, the most cited field study of AI at work.
papers.title: Generative AI at Work

papers.note: Reviews student and teacher assistance, adaptive learning and commercial tools, with the datasets and benchmarks behind each, plus the deployment risks.
papers.title: Large Language Models for Education: A survey and outlook

papers.note: PRISMA review of 159 studies across sectors, the broadest single sweep of GenAI productivity evidence.
papers.title: Enhancing Work Productivity through Generative Artificial Intelligence: A Comprehensive Literature Review

papers.note: Nationally representative US adoption rates, and the finding that firm policy is a main driver of workplace use.
papers.title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI

papers.note: Applies the technology, organization and environment framework to GenAI adoption across 108 organisations.
papers.title: Towards Adoption of Generative AI in Organizational Settings

papers.note: Sector-by-sector account of deployment across healthcare, automotive, finance and education, with the ethical and compute constraints stated alongside.
papers.title: Industrial applications of large language models

papers.note: Warns against treating models as universal text-analysis tools in research, and argues zero-shot use without validation produces unreliable inference.
papers.title: Perils and opportunities in using large language models in psychological research

papers.note: Identifies where models can and cannot help in power systems, and is candid that safety-critical use needs retrieval grounding rather than raw generation.
papers.title: Exploring the Capabilities and Limitations of Large Language Models in the Electric Energy Sector

papers.note: Randomised trials at Microsoft and Accenture across 4,867 developers, 26 percent more completed tasks.
papers.title: The Effects of Generative AI on High-Skilled Work: Evidence from Three Field Experiments with Software Developers

papers.note: Two studies linking task type to where AI actually helps, useful for scoping a use case portfolio.
papers.title: Collaborative AI in the workplace: Enhancing organizational performance through resource-based and task-technology fit perspectives

papers.note: 384 IT managers, finds fairness, accountability and transparency measurably influence whether GenAI gets used at all.
papers.title: Assessing the nexus of Generative AI adoption, ethical considerations and organizational performance

papers.note: Argues against the efficiency only narrative and for human complementary deployment, a useful counterweight in strategy work.
papers.title: Human-AI agency in the age of generative AI

papers.note: 277 B2B managers across seven countries, with ethical leadership moderating the adoption to performance link.
papers.title: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) revolution: A deep dive into GenAI adoption

papers.note: Proposes a staged roadmap from in-context learning to domain fine-tuning for building energy work, and is realistic about data preparation cost.
papers.title: Large language models for building energy applications: Opportunities and challenges

papers.note: Written as a primer for clinicians rather than engineers, and explicit that hallucination and poor generalisation remain blockers to adoption.
papers.title: Large language models in oncology: a review
